risk.provenance_toolCall: From the tool call's permission field, read back from the run.
risk.provenance_toolName: Derived from the tool's name against OpsPilot's static tool registry. The API does not return a risk level on an approval; this is the closest available reading.
risk.provenance_unknown: The API does not return a risk level for this approval, and no tool call was available to read one from. The deterministic explanation below still states what will happen.

explanation.trustedFooter: Derived from the tool's permission class and the arguments below. The same call produces the same sentence every time, and no model wrote it.
explanation.untrustedFooter_before: The model's own justification. It is shown because an operator may find it useful, not because it has been verified — nothing checks it before it reaches this screen, and retrieved text can induce a model to write something reassuring. Weigh the

decision.approveNote: Approving does not run the refund here — it releases the run and the worker performs it.
decision.alreadyDecided_headline: Already decided — this click granted nothing.
decision.alreadyDecided_before: The API returned 409 approval_already_decided: this approval is {state}.
decision.alreadyDecided_after: This is the guard working, not a failure. The decision is a conditional update (`WHERE id = ? AND status = 'pending'`), so the second click found no row to move and no second grant was written. If you have two cards for the same refund, the other one is still pending and still needs its own decision — approving one does not decide the other.
decision.runNotParked_headline: The run is not parked any more, so nothing was decided.
decision.runNotParked_after: A decision only transitions a run that is `waiting_approval`. The run reached this state after the approval was written -- most often because a second card for the same run was decided first, or because the worker reclaimed it.
decision.runMovedOn_headline: The run had already moved on.
decision.runMovedOn_after: The decision was refused before anything was written, because the run was not in the state the transition expects. Open the run to see where it is.
decision.notFound_after: Reload the inbox. An approval decided in another tab leaves the pending filter, so a card left open for a while can point at a row that has moved.
decision.unauthorized_headline: The API rejected the operator token, so nothing was decided.
decision.unauthorized_after: Every request from the dashboard fails while this is true. Set OPSPILOT_OPERATOR_TOKEN in the dashboard's environment to the value the API process was started with, then restart the dev server.
decision.generic_conflict_headline: The API refused this decision with 409 ({code}).
decision.generic_failure_headline: The decision did not go through ({status}).

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: What needs a human right now, what is broken, and what has been happening.
dashboard.waitingHintSome: A tool call that can move money is parked until a person decides. Nothing has been sent.
dashboard.waitingHintNone: Nothing is parked. No risky write is waiting on a decision.
dashboard.failedHintSome: OpsPilot did not finish the job. Open a run to read its failure_reason.
dashboard.failedHintNone: No run has ended in FAILED.
dashboard.replayBody_before: A run resumed after an interruption re-proposes the same refund under a new tool call id, so it holds two pending approvals.
dashboard.replayBody_after: — the idempotency key blocks the replay — but both cards are real and either can be decided. Approving one does not decide the other.
dashboard.rowInFlightHint: Claimed by the worker and moving: received, classifying, retrieving, planning, executing, responding.
dashboard.rowWaitingHint: Parked. The worker released the row; a person has to decide.
dashboard.rowFailedHint: OpsPilot did not finish the job. Each carries a failure_reason.
dashboard.tallyNote_before: Tallied per status from the API, up to its 200-row maximum page. The
dashboard.noRunsHint: Submit a ticket and a run is enqueued for it. The worker claims it on its next poll.
dashboard.zeroChunks: {count} report zero chunks, which means retrieval cannot cite them — a run citing one of them would show no sources.
dashboard.allCitable: Every document has chunks, so every document is citable.

replay.one: One refund is on screen twice.
replay.other: {count} refunds are each on screen twice.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.description_before: Gate 5. A tool call that can move money stops here until a person decides. Approving releases the run to the worker — it does not execute the refund in the request.
approvals.evidenceNote_before: Each card shows the deterministic explanation from the policy engine and the model's own reason, labelled differently.
approvals.evidenceEmphasis: Only the deterministic one is evidence
approvals.evidenceNote_after: — the model's text is untrusted and nothing verifies it before it reaches this screen.

filterHint.pending: Waiting for a decision. This is the inbox.
filterHint.approved: Decided. The run was released to the worker.
filterHint.rejected: Decided. The run went on to an escalation reply.

approvals.emptyPendingTitle: Nothing is waiting for a decision.
approvals.emptyPendingHint: That is a real answer from the API, not an error. A refund proposal parks here; a run that reaches an answer without a risky write never does.
approvals.emptyFilteredHint: Clear the filter to see the pending inbox.

approvalCard.toolCallUnavailable: The run's tool calls were not available to read this call's name from. The arguments below are the API's own snapshot and are still exact.
approvalCard.duplicateIdenticalTitle: This run is showing the same proposal twice.
approvalCard.duplicateDistinctTitle: This run is holding more than one pending approval.
approvalCard.duplicateIdentical_middle: re-proposes the same refund under a new tool call id, so one refund produced
approvalCard.duplicateIdentical_after: — the idempotency key blocks the replay — but both cards are real and both are shown rather than collapsed into one, because hiding one would misreport what the API has pending. Approving this card does not decide the other; it is still waiting and will need its own decision.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.description: Submitting a ticket enqueues an agent run in the same transaction. The worker picks it up on its next poll and it appears in Runs.
tickets.noTicketsHint: Use the form to submit one. A run is enqueued with it, in the same transaction, so a ticket can never exist without having been investigated.

ticketForm.subject: Subject
ticketForm.externalIdHint: Optional. Your own ticket reference. Sending one twice returns 409 ticket_exists rather than creating a duplicate.
ticketForm.bodyPlaceholder: We were charged twice for invoice INV-2026-384. Please investigate and fix it.
ticketForm.createdNote_before: The worker claims it on its next poll, so it will not have moved yet. Watch it on the run page, or reload in a moment. A refund proposal parks for approval — go to
ticketForm.ticketExistsSuffix: — this external_id already has a ticket. Clear the field to create a genuinely new one.

runs.title: Runs
runs.description: Every agent run, newest first. Filter by status to see what is moving, what is parked, and what broke.
runs.emptyFilteredHint: That is a real answer from the API, not an error. Clear the filter to see every run.
runs.emptyUnfilteredHint: A run is created when a ticket is submitted. Nothing here means nothing has been submitted.

run.title: Run detail
run.notFoundBody: The API answered 404. If this id came from another deployment's database it will not exist here.
run.parkedBody_before: The run proposed a tool call that can move money and stopped at the approval gate. The worker has released the row; it will not proceed until someone decides on the
run.parkedBody_after: screen. Approving does not execute the refund inside the request — it makes the run claimable again and the worker performs it.
run.failedCallsStillCompleted: , and this run still reported completed
run.failedCallsListFooter: . If a customer reply is shown, it was composed without these effects.
run.timelineAside: {count} steps, as the server ordered them
run.emptyTimelineUnclaimed: A run writes a step as it works. If it is still `received`, the worker has not claimed it yet.
run.emptyTimelineHeld_before: A worker ({worker}) claimed this run and has not written a step yet.
run.emptyTimelineHeld_after: The claim is held until {until} and is renewed while the worker keeps driving; if it is not renewed, the run becomes claimable again then.
run.emptyTimelineExpired_before: A worker claimed this run, and its claim expired at {until}.
run.emptyTimelineExpired_after: No worker is holding it now — the run becomes claimable again on the next poll.
run.noStepDetail: The server sent no detail for this step type.
run.latencyNotMeasured: Not measured: a state change is a database update, not work the agent did.
run.latencyMissing: The API reported no latency for this step.
run.toolCallsEmptyHint: A run that reaches an answer from retrieved policy alone makes no calls. That is abstention or a policy-only answer, not a failure.
run.sourcesEmptyHint: Abstention is a supported outcome, not an error: the run found no knowledge strong enough to answer from and escalated instead (docs/agent-state-machine.md §3). A completed run with no sources answered from retrieved policy alone only if it cites nothing -- read the timeline to see which.
run.similarityTitle: Cosine similarity between the query and this chunk.
run.replyFailedHint: A failed run does not compose an escalation reply; the failure_reason above says why.
run.replyNoneCompletedHint: The run completed without persisting a response step, so there is nothing to show.
run.replyNonePendingHint: The reply is composed when the run reaches COMPLETED.
run.replyEscalated: Escalated. The run did not complete the request; it handed it to a human. No refund was issued.
run.failureBanner_after: A FAILED run means OpsPilot did not finish the job. Nothing is waiting for approval and nothing will be executed. Read the timeline below for where it stopped.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.description: The documents retrieval can cite. A run can only cite a chunk that is indexed here, so this screen is where 'the agent found nothing' is explained.
knowledge.emptyHint_before: The API reads knowledge/*.md beside src/ in the repository root. With nothing indexed, knowledge.search has nothing to retrieve and a run either abstains or answers from the model alone — press Reindex to ingest the tree.
knowledge.zeroChunkTitle: Zero chunks: retrieval cannot cite this document.
knowledge.noChunksBody: A zero-chunk document is indexed as a row but has nothing to retrieve, so retrieval cannot cite it. That is not an error the API reports — it is visible only here and in a run that returns no sources.

reindex.hint_after: and re-embeds what changed. Unchanged documents are skipped, so repeating it is safe.
reindex.emptyTree_before: No documents were found. The API reads
reindex.emptyTree_after: in the repository root; if that directory is missing or empty there is nothing to index, and retrieval will have nothing to cite.
reindex.zeroIndexedNote: 0 indexed is the expected result here, not a failure.
reindex.zeroIndexedBody: Reindex is idempotent (contract §9): every document was re-hashed, none of the hashes changed, so nothing was re-embedded. The index is up to date. Edit a document and run it again to see a non-zero count.
